About me

Analytical depth. Commercial perspective.

I am drawn to roles where analysis shapes direction: strategy, business analytics, commercial decision support and industry research.

WHO I AM

A modeller who knows the story matters.

With a University of Sydney Bachelor of Commerce background in Business Analytics and Statistics, I work across optimisation, pricing, predictive models and evidence-led research.

What connects my projects is not a single tool. It is the ability to frame an ambiguous question, challenge assumptions, build a defensible analysis and explain what the result means for a decision.

Case 01 · Operations optimisation · Team project

Allocating resources without hiding the cost of service.

G Company’s pilot required rapid replenishment across ten Shanghai stores. Assortment choice changed demand; demand changed capacity; capacity changed which warehouses should open. The analysis had to solve those choices together.

10Pilot storesOperational scope
4Candidate warehousesBinary open/close
31Non-empty assortmentsExhaustive check
4.54%ADE cost reduction vs full rangeModelled comparison
Business story

Variety drives demand—and network cost.

A larger range raises purchase probability but can require more facility capacity and logistics spending.

What I owned

Formulation, heuristic and Excel model.

I built the facility-location formulation, Greedy Algorithm 2 logic and the Solver-ready Excel model.

Decision value

ADE made the trade-off visible.

The ADE option reduced modelled annual logistics cost by 4.54% and slightly increased expected profit per customer versus the full range; these are model estimates, not realised savings.

Capability signal

Structured operational reasoning.

Binary decisions, constraints, sensitivity, heuristic validation and a recommendation operations teams can inspect.

My contribution · 01

Facility-location formulation

Minimised fixed and transport cost subject to one-warehouse assignment, capacity and open-facility constraints.

My contribution · 02

Greedy Algorithm 2

Ordered variants by margin and attractiveness to locate the point where additional variety stopped improving expected profit.

My contribution · 03

Excel Solver model

Linked customer traffic, purchase probability, expected demand, facility capacity and annual cost in an auditable workbook.

Case 02 · Commercial finance · USBS consulting project

From unit cost to a defensible price decision.

A packaging change from HDPE to PEF increased estimated unit cost by AUD 0.17. I modelled how much of that cost could be passed through while keeping the retail increase understandable and commercially defensible.

What I did

Cost pass-through and scenario logic

Compared an estimated AUD 0.17 per-bottle material premium against baseline AUD 9.35 retail price, with alternative pass-through rates and clearly stated demand assumptions.

Capability

Pricing and commercial communication

Explaining how sustainability, affordability and margin protection compete in a real recommendation.

Pass-through simulator
Illustrative new price
Change vs AUD 9.35
Decision framing

This is a scenario tool. A production recommendation would also test elasticity, competitor prices, volume and customer research.

◆ CASE STUDY / EXPANDED VIEW
Case 04 · UNICEF Australia · Team capstone

Turning rare conversion into a contact decision.

The base conversion rate to Regular Giving was about 2.47%. The useful question was not simply “which model scores highest?” It was: who should be contacted, through which channel, under what threshold and cost assumptions?

2.47%Observed positive rateObserved
0.71Full Logistic ROC-AUCValidation
0.52Reduced RF tuned Macro F1Validation
20%Illustrative contact shareScenario, not realised impact
Business story

Contact is scarce and conversion is rare.

Blanket outreach spends budget and risks donor fatigue. A useful model must change who is contacted and how performance is tested.

What I owned

Signals, two models and the impact logic.

I led factor-level EDA, built Logistic Regression and Random Forest models, tuned thresholds, and created the cost and impact estimation strategy.

Decision value

A pilot with measurable guardrails.

Rank high-propensity donors, contact a constrained segment, use holdouts and scale only when incremental conversion and cost remain acceptable.

Capability signal

Cost-aware model-to-action translation.

Imbalanced classification, commercial assumptions, threshold trade-offs, campaign measurement and stakeholder-ready storytelling.

My contribution · 01

Factor screening and EDA

Connected channel, season, first-gift value, demographics and missingness to testable fundraising hypotheses.

My contribution · 02

Logistic + Random Forest

Built interpretable linear and non-linear benchmarks, reduced features and tuned thresholds under severe class imbalance.

My contribution · 03

Cost and impact estimation

Translated contact share, uplift and donor value assumptions into cost, conversion, CPRG and ROI scenarios.

Model classification

A deterministic cohort scenario model with an activity-based cost layer. It estimates planning outcomes under stated assumptions; it is not a causal uplift forecast. The recommended next step is a treatment-versus-holdout pilot measuring incremental RGs, cost per new RG, opt-outs and complaint rates.

Technical note

Threshold tuning changed the operating point. For the reduced Random Forest, recall fell from 0.42 to 0.12 while precision increased from 0.04 to 0.06 and Macro F1 rose from 0.47 to 0.52.

Integrity note

The live simulator uses recurring outreach cost only. One-off implementation was estimated separately using a time–rate model: AUD 8–10k for data pipeline deployment, AUD 6–9k for journey/A/B setup, plus about AUD 2k per quarter for monitoring and recalibration.

Case 05 · R · Individual analysis

From an everyday choice to a testable behavioural question.

The project converted subjective privacy behaviour into measurable variables and tested three questions: whether choices differed by gender, by facility enclosure and by self-reported anxiety.

3Research questionsHypothesis-led
2Significant differencesGender and facility context
1Non-significant resultPrivacy and anxiety
RWrangling + ggplot2Individual analysis
Behavioural story

Physical context may shape privacy choice.

The less-enclosed urinal setting showed a higher preference for the furthest position than stalls.

What I owned

End-to-end individual analysis.

I renamed and recoded variables, built visual comparisons, selected tests, checked assumptions and documented bias.

Decision value

Useful for user research—not universal design claims.

The evidence can generate hypotheses for privacy-sensitive spaces or services, but the student sample limits generalisation.

Capability signal

Hypothesis-led analysis with visual explanation.

I can translate an everyday behaviour into measurable variables, choose an appropriate test, pair the statistic with an interpretable visual and communicate the limits of the sample.

My contribution · 01

Data preparation

Standardised column names, recoded gender, created privacy groups, categorised anxiety and handled missing values.

My contribution · 02

Visual and statistical evidence

Used bar charts, diverging bars, heatmaps, boxplots, density plots, chi-square tests and a Wilcoxon rank-sum test.

My contribution · 03

Bias and limitation review

Documented selection, classification, measurement, independence and survey-design risks.

◆ CASE STUDY / EXPANDED VIEW
Case 06 · eClinicalMedicine · Published 2025

Finding connected risks in 15 national surveys.

Developmental delay, functional disability and undernutrition are often analysed separately. The paper asked how they co-occur among children aged 36–59 months and which child, maternal and household factors are associated with each pattern.

50,709Children analysedSurvey-weighted research
15Sub-Saharan African countries2017–2022 MICS
5Latent classesCo-occurrence patterns
3rdAuthor positionPublished collaboration
Research story

Three vulnerabilities interact.

Analysing each condition alone can miss groups experiencing overlapping developmental, functional and nutritional burdens.

What I contributed

Topic development, data cleaning and discussion.

I supported the research question, data cleaning and structuring, and contributed to the discussion and first-draft writing.

Policy value

Integrated intervention, not siloed response.

The findings support combined early screening, rehabilitation, inclusive education, nutrition support and assistance for mothers facing disability or low education.

Capability signal

Research collaboration at publication standard.

Multi-country data, evidence synthesis, careful interpretation, written argument and collaboration across Tsinghua, Karolinska and Sydney.

Publication

Co-occurrence and associated factors of developmental delay, functional disability, and undernutrition in early childhood.

Yan C, Zhao S, Cui J, Shangguan S, Wang Z, Tang K. eClinicalMedicine. 2025;85:103305.

Read published paper ↗
Research integrity

The study is cross-sectional and identifies associations, not causal effects. The portfolio therefore frames the value as policy prioritisation and integrated programme design.

Interactive evidence

Explore the five co-occurrence classes

Select a class to compare outcome probabilities, then inspect associated risk-factor findings.

Technical note

The paper used Latent Class Analysis to identify patterns and survey-weighted multinomial logistic regression to examine associated factors. Sensitivity analyses addressed ECDI measurement differences and missing data.
